name: Legal obsolescence

subjectOf.text: Legal garbage collection is stipulated as the systematic review and removal of outdated, redundant, or otherwise unnecessary laws from the legal code, by analogy to garbage collection in computer science.
subjectOf.abstract: Legal garbage collection refers to the systematic review and removal of outdated, redundant, or otherwise unnecessary laws from the legal code.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Future of Law - Dynamic Web3 Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4957318

subjectOf.text: Obsolescence in the WDAG system is expressed as gradual loss of weight rather than deletion, which keeps rules revisitable if circumstances change and avoids hasty or ill considered removal decisions.
subjectOf.abstract: Instead, less relevant rules gradually lose weight, allowing them to be revisited if circumstances change, thus maintaining institutional relevance while avoiding hasty or ill-considered decisions.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Future of Law - Dynamic Web3 Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4957318
scope_conditions: where relevance is a continuous weight rather than a binary in force status
